FLUSH1:
MOV     AH, 01h          ; BIOS: is a key waiting?
INT     16h
JZ      EMPTY1           ; ZF = 1: the buffer is empty
MOV     AH, 00h          ; take the key out
INT     16h
JMP     FLUSH1
EMPTY1:
XOR     BX, BX           ; keys stored so far
STORE1:
MOV     AH, 05h
MOV     CX, 3920h        ; the space bar: scan 39h, ASCII 20h
INT     16h
TEST    AL, AL           ; 0 = stored, 1 = full
JNZ     FULL1
INC     BX
CMP     BX, 20           ; a safety stop
JB      STORE1
FULL1:
MOV     AX, BX
CALL    PDEC             ; 15
MOV     DX, OFFSET FIT1
MOV     AH, 09h          ; DOS: print the $-string at DS:DX
INT     21h
DRAIN1:
MOV     AH, 01h          ; empty the buffer again
INT     16h
JZ      DONE1
MOV     AH, 00h
INT     16h
JMP     DRAIN1
DONE1:

FIT1    DB      " keys fit in the buffer$"
PDEC    PROC    NEAR     ; print AX in decimal; keeps every register
PUSH    AX
PUSH    BX
PUSH    CX
PUSH    DX
MOV     BX, 10
XOR     CX, CX           ; digits on the stack
DECD1:
XOR     DX, DX
DIV     BX               ; AX = AX / 10, DX = the last digit
PUSH    DX
INC     CX
TEST    AX, AX
JNZ     DECD1
DECD2:
POP     DX               ; the digits come back first to last
ADD     DL, "0"
MOV     AH, 02h
INT     21h
LOOP    DECD2
POP     DX
POP     CX
POP     BX
POP     AX
RET
PDEC    ENDP
